record.paper_title: A review of four decades of time-dependent scheduling: main results, new topics, and open problems
record.context_brief: Two-machine open shop with proportional-linear operations
record.original_question: Given a two-machine open shop in which each job has one operation on each machine and operation i of job j has proportional-linear time-dependent processing time p_ij(t) = b_ij(a + b t) when it starts at time t, with common constants a and b and operation-specific coefficient b_ij, determine the computational complexity of minimizing total completion time sum_j C_j. Is this problem NP-hard at least in the ordinary sense, or can it be solved in polynomial time?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a two-machine open shop scheduling problem defined as follows. There are $n$ jobs $J_1, \ldots, J_n$, each of which must be processed once on machine $M_1$ and once on machine $M_2$, in either order, with no two operations of the same job overlapping in time and no machine processing two operations simultaneously. Let constants $a \ge 0$ and $b \ge 0$ be given (not both zero), and for each job $j$ and each machine $i \in \{1,2\}$ let $b_{ij} > 0$ be a given coefficient. If operation $i$ of job $j$ starts at time $t$, then its processing time is the time-dependent (proportional-linear) function
$$p_{ij}(t) = b_{ij}(a + b t).$$
Let $C_j$ denote the completion time of job $j$ in a feasible schedule. The objective is to find a schedule minimizing the total completion time $\sum_{j=1}^n C_j$.

Determine the computational complexity of this problem: is it NP-hard (at least in the ordinary sense), or does it admit a polynomial-time algorithm?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a complexity classification (polynomial algorithm or NP-hardness proof) for the two-machine open-shop problem with proportional-linear processing times $p_{ij}(t)=b_{ij}(a+bt)$ and total completion time objective. Related results address makespan or proportionate variants, but the specific status of this problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: On the complexity of proportionate open shop and job shop problems
status_evidence.snippet: Studies complexity of proportionate open/job shop problems, including NP-hardness proofs and polynomial algorithms for various criteria, but without addressing the time-dependent proportional-linear case for total completion time.
status_evidence.claim: Closely related complexity work does not resolve the proportional-linear time-dependent variant with sum of completion times.

status_evidence.title: Proportionate and Ordered Open Shops
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of proportionate open shops; does not give a complexity classification for the two-machine open shop with p_ij(t)=b_ij(a+bt) and sum C_j.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the targeted problem found in proportionate open shop literature.
